units.title: The 80/20 ADHF Split, Eight Risk Factors, Four Clinical Classes and Mild-to-Moderate ADHF
units.sec: The 80/20 ADHF Split, Eight Risk Factors, Four Clinical Classes and Mild-to-Moderate ADHF
units.guide:
ADHF is 80% prior HF (HFrEF/HFpEF, NYHA 1/2) and 20% de novo (p326). Risk factors, in order, are patient-related factors, infections (LRTI/IE), anemia, drugs (NSAIDs), MI, AF, uncontrolled HTN and pregnancy.
Four classes are mild-to-moderate ADHF, hypertensive ADHF, ADHF with acute pulmonary edema and cardiogenic shock.
Mild-to-moderate disease is 70% of ADHF, underlies HFrEF and is precipitated by LRTI; progressive dyspnea joins right-sided JVP/tender liver/edema, without pulmonary edema or shock, and O/E may show S3, cardiomegaly and MR from annular dilatation.

units.title: Oral Diuretics, Hypertensive ADHF and the Symptoms and Signs of Acute Pulmonary Edema
units.sec: Oral Diuretics, Hypertensive ADHF and the Symptoms and Signs of Acute Pulmonary Edema
units.guide:
Mild-to-moderate ADHF uses oral torsemide 5–10 mg (p327). Hypertensive ADHF is most common in females with underlying HFpEF; it has progressive dyspnea, uncontrolled HTN, diastolic-failure symptoms and still no pulmonary edema or shock, and is managed with IV diuretics plus oral antihypertensives.
Acute pulmonary edema causes breathlessness worsening over 60–90 minutes, an upright patient unable to lie down, gasping/air hunger and diaphoresis. Signs are tachypnea >30 bpm, hypertensive crisis, crepts across all lung fields and frothy sputum ± hemoptysis.

units.title: The Five Differential Diagnoses, Emergency Imaging, the Kerley-Line Table and the Perfusion–Congestion Flowchart
units.sec: The Five Differential Diagnoses, Emergency Imaging, the Kerley-Line Table and the Perfusion–Congestion Flowchart
units.guide:
The differential list is ACS; acute AR (dissection, ruptured sinus of Valsalva, IE) or acute MR; myocarditis; bilateral renal-artery stenosis → flash pulmonary edema; and Takotsubo cardiomyopathy (p328).
CXR is not done in an emergency, but bat-wing appearance indicates cardiopulmonary edema; cephalisation of pulmonary vessels is the earliest finding and is associated with Kerley A/B/C lines. Kerley A is LAP 12–19 mmHg with dilated anastomotic lymphatics; B is 20–24 mmHg with septal fluid and short horizontal lines perpendicular to pleura; C is 20–24 mmHg with reticular/enface B lines; LAP >25 mmHg means acute pulmonary edema.
The flowchart separates stable from no, then low perfusion at rest from no (hypovolemia); warm/dry is normal PCWP/CI, warm/wet elevated PCWP/normal CI, cold/dry low-normal PCWP/reduced CI and cold/wet elevated PCWP/reduced CI. Natriuretic peptides/nesiritide or nitroprusside/nitroglycerin, inotropes and pulmonary edema + cardiogenic shock label the treatment paths.

units.title: The Acute-Pulmonary-Edema Treatment Bundle and Cardiogenic-Shock Features, Investigations and Phenotype-Specific Support
units.sec: The Acute-Pulmonary-Edema Treatment Bundle and Cardiogenic-Shock Features, Investigations and Phenotype-Specific Support
units.guide:
Acute pulmonary edema management uses IV furosemide 360 mg split 100 + 100 + 100 + 60 mg, semi-recumbent 45°, high-flow O₂ by NRBM/NIV, morphine 4 mg IV for extravascular fluid shift and BP control with NTG 5 µg/min (p329).
Cardiogenic shock has narrow pulse pressure with SBP <90 mmHg, fatigue, altered mentation, cyanosis and cold extremities, with a poor-prognosis note. Lactic acid rules out occult shock; early ECHO excludes ACS-related acute AR/MR.
HFrEF support uses dobutamine (common inotrope), milrinone (common inodilator) and IABP/ECMO; HFpEF uses vasopressors vasopressin/desmopressin.

units.title: Non-Recovering Pulmonary Edema, SCUF, BNP/NT-proBNP and Early Vasodilator Therapy in Acute AR or MR
units.sec: Non-Recovering Pulmonary Edema, SCUF, BNP/NT-proBNP and Early Vasodilator Therapy in Acute AR or MR
units.guide:
If pulmonary edema with maintained BP is not recovering, the page offers dialysis or SCUF via central/femoral catheter; SCUF is expanded as slow continuous ultrafiltration (p330).
BNP/NT-proBNP >900 pg/mL is printed for patients with probability of HF; values are lower in obesity because of adipocyte metabolism, and the note flags diagnostic value in renal failure.
Early vasodilator therapy for acute AR/MR prefers nitroprusside > NTG (nitroglycerine); the printed chain is reduced aortic pressure → reduced transvalvular gradient.
